documents.unit: UTMB Legal Affairs, Compliance, Information Security, Information Services
documents.title: UTMB Artificial Intelligence (AI) Joint Policy
documents.summary: UTMB's joint policy, adapted from UT Austin, leaves course AI rules to schools and instructors and says that without a syllabus statement AI counts like help from another person or an uncited source. Its firmest rules cover data: no confidential data, FERPA records or health information in public AI tools. Students are responsible for AI content, must verify it and cite it, and nondisclosure violates the conduct policy.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no default allow or ban for coursework: "students must abide by AI policies or statements for the UTMB schools and courses" and "Faculty are strongly encouraged to develop their own policies ... allowing or disallowing some or all uses". Its fixed prohibitions concern data and non-public output, not a course-level stance, so delegates.

units.why: The sentence tells 'faculty and staff' using AI 'for clinical or administrative work' to 'be mindful of the security implications of information shared with AI tools', a duty about data protection, so P50. 'Should' makes it a recommendation, and it is a caution without a restriction of its own, so neutral.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A ta-staff, B instructor), phase (A during-work, B general) and unit_stance (A neutral, B restrict). The audience is faculty and staff together; the codebook has no joint value, so instructor (faculty named first) is used and the staff half is noted. The work is actual use of AI tools, so during-work. 'Should be mindful' sets no limit, so neutral.

units.why: "entering such information into the public ChatGPT web interface is not in compliance with UTMB or UT System policies" forbids a specific data practice, so P50 (protect confidential data) rather than P77.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed only on phase (A during-work, B general). Entering information into the public ChatGPT interface is an act of use, so during-work. Both coded P50 must-not prohibit.

units.why: 'any use of ChatGPT or similar AI Tools cannot use any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information unless a university contract is in place' bans sensitive data in AI tools with one exception, so P50, must-not, and restrict because of the exception.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A during-work, B general) and unit_stance (A prohibit, B restrict). Use of AI tools with sensitive data is an act of use, so during-work. The ban is lifted when a university contract protects the data, so restrict, not prohibit. Both noted the exception; notes merged.

units.policy: Any use of ChatGPT or similar AI tools cannot use any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information unless a university contract is in place that protects such university data from being used for training models or isolates it in a separate instance not accessible to external parties.
units.fit_note: Also allows an exception where a university contract protects the data from model training or isolates it; P50 (protect data, prefer vetted tools) does not capture the contract exception.

units.why: "student records subject to FERPA, health information, proprietary information ... must not be used with AI Tools" lists protected data classes; P50 fits.

units.why: 'must not be used to generate output that would be considered non-public' is a general ban on a category of AI output, with examples listed in the next units; no type covers a ban defined by non-public status, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded the umbrella sentence; B coded only the listed examples. It is a real rule that frames the examples (unpublished research, legal analysis or advice, personnel decisions, academic work, materials, grading), so kept. Phase set to general to match the examples it frames. 'Legal analysis or advice' is an example covered here and not coded separately.
units.anchor: must not be used to generate output that would be considered non-public
units.frag_start: Similarly, ChatGPT or similar AI Tools
units.uncovered_note: AI tools may not be used to generate output that would be considered non-public (unpublished research, legal advice, and similar).

units.anchor: generating proprietary or unpublished research

units.why: 'ChatGPT or similar AI Tools must not be used to generate output that would be considered non-public. Examples ... and grading' bans AI grading; grading is the instructor's task, so actor instructor, and P46 (humans, not AI, assign grades) fits.
units.resolution_why: A coded grading as its own unit (P46, instructor, during-work); B merged grading with instructional materials and coded actor all, phase general. Grading and creating non-public materials are two distinct rules, so they are separate units (as in A). Actor instructor because grading is the instructor's work; phase general to match the other items in the same list. Type P46 as both.

units.policy: ChatGPT or similar AI Tools must not be used for grading.

units.why: The list of non-public output includes 'creation of non-public instructional materials', which bans AI for an instructor's teaching work, so P59, actor instructor, must-not.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A split this out; B merged it with grading. Distinct rule, so kept as its own unit. Phase set to general like the other list items.

units.policy: ChatGPT or similar AI Tools must not be used for creation of non-public instructional materials.

units.why: 'completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor' bans AI use for coursework beyond what the instructor allows; the rule is tied to the instructor's permission, so P04 with a fit note, actor student, restrict.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A student, B all), phase (A during-work, B general) and type (A P04, B P19). The source bans academic work done with AI 'in a manner not allowed by the instructor': the ban exists only to the extent the instructor sets it, so P04 fits better than P19, which says not to have AI produce submitted work outright. The ban binds students, so actor student. Phase general to match the list it comes from.

units.why: "may not be used for any activity that would be illegal, fraudulent or a violation of any state or federal law, or UTMB or UT System policies" is a rule to follow law and policy (P77); P74 was not chosen because the rule is general compliance. units.resolution_why: Both coded P52 informs; B noted it is about contractual liability for terms of use, not copyright or ownership. P52 is a stretch, so UNCOVERED with a note.

notes: Single university-layer document, partly adapted from UT Austin; no school or computing documents found. The sentence barring AI use for illegal or fraudulent activity appears twice and is coded once; the student-section restatement of the non-public-output sentence is not coded separately. The listed non-public output example 'legal analysis or advice' is covered by the umbrella unit and not coded separately. Web page chrome skipped.
